Build and render a table

lm_tab.Rd

lm_tab() describes a table: formatted cells, column alignment, optional group (panel) rows, a title and notes. lm_render() turns it into plain text, GitHub markdown, LaTeX (booktabs) or HTML, and optionally writes it to a file. Every lm_table() method builds an lm_tab and renders it; packages that add methods (such as latentclasscausal) can do the same.

Usage

lm_tab(
  body,
  title = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  align = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  bold = NULL,
  digits = 3,
  bold_note = NULL
)

lm_render(
  tab,
  format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
  file = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lm_table_output'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm_table_output'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm_tab'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

body

Data frame (or character matrix) of cells. Numeric columns are formatted with digits; character columns are used as they are (NA becomes empty). Trailing *s in a cell are rendered as superscript stars in LaTeX and HTML.

title

Optional title (caption).

notes

Optional character vector of notes printed under the table, one per line.

align

Column alignment, "l", "c" or "r" per column (recycled; default: first column left, others right).

groups

Optional character vector, one per row: a new panel heading is printed whenever the value changes (NA or "": none), and the rows of a panel are indented.

bold

Optional logical matrix (same shape as body): cells set in bold (not in text output).

digits

Number of decimals for numeric columns of body.

bold_note

Note explaining the bold cells; added to notes when some cell is bold, except in text output, which has no bold.

tab

An lm_tab object.

format

"text" (UTF-8 rules, for the console), "markdown" (GitHub), "latex" (booktabs; needs \usepackage{booktabs}) or "html".

file

Optional path; the table is written there (UTF-8) and returned invisibly.

label

LaTeX \label{} (LaTeX only).

x

An lm_table_output or lm_tab object.

...

Ignored.

Value

lm_tab(): an object of class lm_tab, a list with cells (character matrix), header, align, title, notes, groups, bold and bold_note. Its print method prints the text rendering.

lm_render(): an object of class lm_table_output, a character string (with attribute format) that prints as the table; returned invisibly when written to file. as.character() drops the class and attribute. The print methods return x invisibly (print.lm_tab() returns the rendered text).

Details

Cells are escaped for the target format (markdown * and |; LaTeX special characters, <, >, and the Greek and superscript characters used by the package; HTML &, <, >). Trailing *s in a cell are significance stars: superscripts in LaTeX and HTML. Text output uses UTF-8 rules and cannot show bold. LaTeX output is a complete table float and needs \usepackage{booktabs}; HTML output uses inline styles only. Written files are UTF-8.

In R Markdown and Quarto documents, an lm_table_output is emitted as is (through a knit_print method registered when knitr is installed), so use format = "markdown", "html" or "latex" to match the output format and set the chunk option results = "asis" if needed.

See also

lm_table(), lm_format_num()

Examples

tab <- lm_tab(data.frame(Model = c("A", "B"), BIC = c(1012.3, 1009.8)),
              title = "Fit", notes = "Lower is better.",
              bold = cbind(FALSE, c(FALSE, TRUE)), bold_note = "Lowest BIC in bold.")
tab
#> Fit
#> ───────────────
#> Model       BIC
#> ───────────────
#> A      1012.300
#> B      1009.800
#> ───────────────
#> Lower is better.
lm_render(tab, "markdown")
#> **Fit**
#> 
#> | Model | BIC |
#> | :--- | ---: |
#> | A | 1012.300 |
#> | B | **1009.800** |
#> 
#> *Lower is better.*  
#> *Lowest BIC in bold.*  
lm_render(tab, "latex", label = "tab:fit")
#> % requires \usepackage{booktabs}
#> \begin{table}[htbp]
#> \centering
#> \caption{Fit}
#> \label{tab:fit}
#> \begin{tabular}{lr}
#> \toprule
#> Model & BIC \\
#> \midrule
#> A & 1012.300 \\
#> B & \textbf{1009.800} \\
#> \bottomrule
#> \end{tabular}
#> \par\smallskip
#> \parbox{\linewidth}{\footnotesize Lower is better. \\ Lowest BIC in bold.}
#> \end{table}
lm_render(tab, "html")
#> <table class="lm-table" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-top:2px solid #000;border-bottom:2px solid #000;">
#> <caption style="caption-side:top;text-align:left;font-weight:bold;padding-bottom:4px;">Fit</caption>
#> <thead>
#> <tr><th style="text-align:left;padding:2px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid #000;">Model</th><th style="text-align:right;padding:2px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid #000;">BIC</th></tr>
#> </thead>
#> <tbody>
#> <tr><td style="text-align:left;padding:2px 8px;">A</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:2px 8px;">1012.300</td></tr>
#> <tr><td style="text-align:left;padding:2px 8px;">B</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:2px 8px;"><strong>1009.800</strong></td></tr>
#> </tbody>
#> <tfoot>
#> <tr><td colspan="2" style="text-align:left;font-size:90%;border-top:1px solid #000;padding:4px 8px;">Lower is better.<br>Lowest BIC in bold.</td></tr>
#> </tfoot>
#> </table>
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tex")
lm_render(tab, "latex", file = f)
readLines(f)[1:3]
#> [1] "% requires \\usepackage{booktabs}" "\\begin{table}[htbp]"             
#> [3] "\\centering"
